question.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(1,-2)$ and which passes through the point $(-3,6)?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(1,-2),$ and so we have

$$
x-1=2pt,\,y+2=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-3,6),$ we can substitute $x=-3$ and $y=6$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-4=2pt \\ 8=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{2}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8 & =p{(-\frac{2}{p})}^{2} \\ 8 & =p\cdot \frac{4}{{p}^{2}} \\ 8 & =\frac{4}{p} \\ p & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x-1=2(\frac{1}{2})t,\,y-(-2)=(\frac{1}{2}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x-1=t,\,y+2=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}.
$$
